tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

# web/ (Court frontend): orientation report for a new reviewer

Repo: `/home/agentops/dev/kleros/kleros-v2/web`. The current branch is `feature/shutter-reveal-justification/shutter-reveal-justification-001`, which is `dev` plus one web commit (`e19cf9f1`). All paths below are relative to `web/` unless marked absolute.

**Stack:**
- React 18, Vite, react-router v6 with HashRouter-style URLs (`/#/...`).
- styled-components v5.
- wagmi v2 + viem, Reown AppKit for wallets.
- TanStack Query v5, with GraphQL through a batcher (`src/context/GraphqlBatcher.tsx`).
- i18next with `en`, `es`, `fr`.
- `@kleros/ui-components-library` **^2.20.0**.

**Generated code is not committed:**
- `src/hooks/contracts/generated.ts` comes from wagmi (`yarn generate:hooks`).
- `src/graphql/**` comes from graphql-codegen (`yarn generate:gql`).
- Both are gitignored and currently absent, so `yarn generate` must run before typecheck or tests.

---

## 1. Feature pages (`src/pages`)

Routing lives in `src/app.tsx`. Every top-level page is `React.lazy` inside `<Suspense fallback={<Loader/>}>`, except `AttachmentDisplay`, which is imported eagerly.

Provider stack: StyledComponents → ErrorBoundary → Web3 → QueryClient → GraphqlBatcher → Atlas → IsList → NewDispute → Language.

There is **no "Dashboard" page**. It was renamed to **Profile** (`/profile`).

**Home (`/`) — `pages/Home/index.tsx`**
- Wrapped in `HomePageProvider`, which calls `useHomePageQuery(oneYearAgo)` in `hooks/useHomePageContext.tsx`.
- `CourtOverview/`:
  - `Stats` uses `useCoinPrice` and `useIsDesktop`.
  - Chart.js charts: `TimeSeriesChart`, `StakedPNKByCourtsChart`, `CasesByCourtsChart`.
  - `ExtraStats` uses `useHomePageExtraStats(range)`.
- `components/LatestCases` calls `useCasesQuery(0, 3, filters)`.
- `TopJurors/` calls `useJurorsByCoherenceScore(0, 5, "coherenceScore", "desc")` and has Desktop/Mobile card variants.
- `Community/` renders static links from `consts/community-elements.ts`.

**Cases list (`/cases/display/:page/:order/:filter`) — `pages/Cases/CasesFetcher.tsx`**
- `filter` is a URI-encoded JSON filter (`decodeURIFilter` / `useRootPath` in `utils/uri.ts`).
- Page size is 9 on desktop and 3 on mobile.
- Hooks: `useCasesQuery`, `useCounterQuery`, `useCourtDetails`.
- `calculateStats` derives total and ruled counts from global counters, or from court counters when a court filter is set.
- It renders `components/CasesDisplay`.

**CaseDetails (`/cases/:id/*`) — `pages/Cases/CaseDetails/index.tsx`**
- Wraps everything in `VotingContextProvider` (`hooks/useVotingContext.tsx`) and `ClassicAppealProvider` (`hooks/useClassicAppealContext.tsx`).
- Header shows `CaseStarButton` and `MaintenanceButtons/`: PassPeriod, Draw, SetJurors, ExecuteRuling, DistributeRewards, WithdrawAppealFees. These use the older simulate+write+`wrapWithToast` pattern.
- Also renders `Timeline.tsx` and `Tabs.tsx`. The Appeal tab is disabled when the period index is below 3 with only one round, or when it is the last round (`isLastRound(appealCost)`).
- **Overview** (`Overview/index.tsx`):
  - Hooks: `usePopulatedDisputeData(id, arbitrable)` (fetches the template, runs SDK data mappings, then `populateTemplate`), `useDisputeDetailsQuery`, `useCourtPolicy`, `useVotingHistory`.
  - Renders `DisputeContext`, `Verdict`, `DisputeInfo` and `Policies`.
  - Kit-specific extra info comes from `useDisputeKitInfo(...).OverviewExtraInfo`. For token-gated kits this is `Overview/DisputeKitOverviewExtraInfo/gated.tsx`, which uses `useGatedTokenInfo` and has hard-coded English strings such as "Token Gated".
- **Evidence** (`Evidence/index.tsx`):
  - Hooks: `useEvidences(id, debouncedSearch)` (500 ms debounce), `useSpamEvidence`, `usePopulatedDisputeData`.
  - Spam evidence can be hidden or shown.
  - Arbitrable-provided `extraEvidences` render first.
  - `SubmitEvidenceModal.tsx` handles submission.
  - The route renders `<Evidence />` **without the `arbitrable` prop**, and the `usePopulatedDisputeData` query key (`["DisputeTemplate", disputeID]`) does not include the arbitrable address. Its cache entry (staleTime Infinity) is shared with Overview, so whichever tab loads first decides the populated data.
- **Voting** (`Voting/index.tsx`):
  - Resolves the dispute-kit config by address and renders `disputeKitInfo.VotingComponent` (Classic or Shutter), gated by drawn, commit/vote period and not-yet-voted.
  - Otherwise it shows `VotingHistory` and `VotesDetails/`.
  - `Classic/` switches between Commit, Reveal and Vote using `isHiddenVotes` and `isCommitPeriod`.
  - `Shutter/` switches between Commit and Reveal. Reveal is automatic (`hasAutomaticVoteReveal`).
  - `ConfirmVoteModal.tsx` (react-modal) is the new pre-vote/commit confirmation.
  - The success Popup is `VOTE_WITH_COMMIT` or `VOTE_WITHOUT_COMMIT`.
- **Appeal** (`Appeal/index.tsx`):
  - In the appeal period it renders `disputeKitInfo.AppealComponent`. Every kit currently uses `Appeal/Classic` (Options/StageOne and StageTwo, `Fund.tsx`, which uses `useFundAppeal`).
  - Otherwise it renders `AppealHistory`.
  - An unknown kit shows `InfoCard` with `alerts.unsupported_dispute_kit`; while the address is unknown it shows a Skeleton.

**Courts (`/courts/:id/*`, default `1`) — `pages/Courts/CourtDetails/index.tsx`**
- `useCourtTree` drives the breadcrumb (`getCourtsPath`).
- Renders `StakePanel` (see §3), `Stats/` and `Description.tsx` (court policy via `useCourtPolicy`), plus `LatestCases` filtered by court.
- `JurorsStakedByCourt/` uses `useTopStakedJurorsByCourt`. `StakingHistoryByCourt/` uses `useStakingEventsByCourt` against Atlas.
- `TopSearch.tsx` hosts the court search and the `StakeMaintenanceButton/` dotted menu (Phase, PassPhase, ExecuteDelayedStake). The URL hash `#maintenance` opens it.
- `ClaimPnkButton` (faucet) appears only when `!isProductionDeployment()`.

**Profile (`/profile/{stakes/:page | cases/:page/:order/:filter | votes/...}?address=`) — `pages/Profile/index.tsx`**
- The `?address=` param is validated with `isAddress`. If it is missing, the page redirects to the connected address.
- `JurorCard/` uses `useUserQuery` and shows level, coherence and rewards. `StakingRewards.tsx` contains commented-out code.
- `Stakes/`:
  - Current stakes from `useJurorStakeDetailsQuery` plus `useReadSortitionModuleGetJurorBalance(address, 1)` for total and locked stake.
  - `StakingHistory` from `useStakingEventsByCourt` (Atlas; disabled on local deployment).
- `Cases/` uses `useMyCasesQuery` and `useUserQuery` and reuses `CasesDisplay`.
- `Votes/`:
  - `useAllUserDraws` fetches every draw in batches to get past the 1000-item limit. The draws are grouped per round and paginated on the client.
  - `useUserDrawsCount` feeds the stats.
- The page also renders `FavoriteCases`.

**Resolver (`/resolver/*`) — `pages/Resolver/index.tsx`**
- Access is gated by `isConnected`, then `EnsureAuth` (Atlas SIWE sign-in).
- Wizard steps:
  - `create`: `Landing/`, which is "from scratch" or "duplicate an existing case by ID". Duplicating pulls `useDisputeDetailsQuery`, `usePopulatedDisputeData` and `useRoundDetailsQuery`, and reads gated token info from the extradata.
  - Then `title`, `description`, `court` (`Parameters/Court` with `FeatureSelection`), `category`, `jurors` (reads `arbitrationCost` with `prepareArbitratorExtradata`), `voting-options`, `notable-persons`, `policy` (Atlas `uploadFile`), and `preview` (`Preview/`, `BatchCreationCard`).
- State lives in `context/NewDisputeContext.tsx` and persists to localStorage (`disputeData`, `disputeBatchSize`). It resets when navigating outside `/resolver` or `/attachment`.
- `constructDisputeTemplate` builds the template JSON. It hex-encodes answer ids **by mutating them in place** and injects the arbitrator address and chain.
- Submission:
  - `NavigationButtons/SubmitDisputeButton.tsx` calls `useSimulateDisputeResolverCreateDisputeForTemplate`, then write, then `wrapWithToast`, then `retrieveDisputeIdFromLogs`, then the `DISPUTE_CREATED` Popup. `isTemplateValid` lives here.
  - `SubmitBatchDisputesButton.tsx` uses `useTransactionBatcher`.
- Feature and dispute-kit selection:
  - Logic is in `src/dispute-kits/disputeFeature.ts` (`toggleFeature`, `findMatchingKits`, `ensureValidSmart`, `getDisabledOptions`, `resolveInitialFeatureSet`, `getDisputeKitsForDeployment`).
  - Supported kits per court come from `useSupportedDisputeKits`.
  - UI pieces are in `components/DisputeFeatures/`.

**GetPnk (`/get-pnk`) — `pages/GetPnk/`**
- `Widget.tsx` embeds a LI.FI swap/bridge widget (`@lifi/widget`), themed from styled-components.
- `WalletProvider.tsx` creates a separate AppKit and Wagmi adapter (mainnet, arbitrum, arbitrumSepolia) synced with `useSyncWagmiConfig`.
- `ClaimPnkButton` appears on non-production deployments.

**Settings (`/settings/email-confirmation`) — `pages/Settings/EmailConfirmation/index.tsx`**
- Calls `useAtlasProvider().confirmEmail({address, token})` from the search params and shows confirmed, invalid-token or error states.
- The notification settings UI itself lives in the header menu: `src/layout/Header/navbar/Menu/Settings/Notifications/FormContactDetails/` handles email subscribe and the new unsubscribe flow with a confirmation step.
- `context/AtlasProvider.tsx` wraps `@kleros/kleros-app`'s AtlasProvider (`SignupProduct.CourtV2`, `IpfsProduct.CourtV2`).

**Jurors leaderboard (`/jurors/:page/:order/:filter`) — `pages/Jurors/`**
- `useTotalLeaderboardJurors` plus `DisplayJurors.tsx` (`useJurorsByCoherenceScore` with paging and ordering), `Search.tsx` and `StatsAndFilters.tsx`.

**AttachmentDisplay (`/attachment?url=`) — `pages/AttachmentDisplay/`**
- Renders `components/FileViewer`, recently hardened to http/https URLs only and routed through `utils/urlValidation.ts`.

---

## 2. Shared components (`src/components`)

**Case cards and lists**
- `DisputeView/index.tsx`: case card-or-list switch based on `useIsList()` (`context/IsListProvider.tsx`, persisted in localStorage). It fetches `usePopulatedDisputeData` and `useCourtPolicy` per item and exports `getPeriodEndTimestamp`.
- `DisputeView/DisputeCardView.tsx` and `DisputeListView.tsx`: grid card and redesigned list row.
- `DisputeView/CardLabels/`: user-specific labels (drawn, voted, funded, rewards).
- `DisputeView/PeriodBanner.tsx`: coloured period strip.
- `DisputeView/DisputeInfo/`: court, category, rewards and round fields.
- `CasesDisplay/`: title, `Search`, `StatsAndFilters` (list/grid toggle and filters), and `CasesGrid` (pagination plus skeletons).
- `LatestCases.tsx`: 3 latest cases, optionally filtered.
- `FavoriteCases.tsx` / `CaseStarButton.tsx`: starred cases via `hooks/useStarredCases`.

**Case content**
- `Verdict/`:
  - `index.tsx` shows `FinalDecision` (current ruling from `useReadKlerosCoreCurrentRuling`, plus voting-context buttons).
  - `DisputeTimeline.tsx` is the ruling timeline.
- `DisputePreview/`:
  - `DisputeContext.tsx` shows question, answers and aliases. It is shared by Overview and the Resolver Preview.
  - `Policies.tsx` shows the dispute policy, court policy and attachment links.
  - `Alias.tsx` renders a party alias.
- `EvidenceCard.tsx`: evidence item (markdown, file link, sender `JurorLink`, tx explorer link).
- `MarkdownRenderer.tsx` / `MarkdownEditor.tsx`: rehype-sanitize allowlist, plus `ExternalLinkWarning.tsx` modal for unsafe or external URLs.
- `FileViewer/`: doc viewer with Markdown and SVG viewers.

**Stats and fields**
- `Field.tsx`: icon, label and value, with an optional internal link.
- `StatDisplay.tsx`: stat tile.
- `ExtraStatsDisplay.tsx`: extra stat row.
- `NumberDisplay.tsx`: number with tooltip.
- `InfoCard.tsx`: info-circle message box (`msg`).
- `WithHelpTooltip.tsx`: tooltip wrapper.
- `Tag.tsx`: toggle tag (used for Stake/Withdraw).

**Popups and modals**
- `Popup/index.tsx`: post-transaction success popup with a discriminated `PopupType`: `STAKE_WITHDRAW`, `APPEAL`, `VOTE_WITH_COMMIT`, `VOTE_WITHOUT_COMMIT`, `DISPUTE_CREATED`, `SWAP_SUCCESS`.
- `Popup/MiniGuides/*`: "How it works" guides (Staking, Appeal, BinaryVoting, RankedVoting, DisputeResolver, Onboarding, JurorLevels), opened through `HowItWorks.tsx`.
- `Overlay.tsx` / `OverlayPortal.tsx` with `hooks/useLockOverlayScroll`.
- react-modal is also used directly, for example in `ConfirmVoteModal`.

**Wallet and auth**
- `ConnectWallet/`: AppKit open or switch chain.
- `EnsureChain.tsx`: renders children only when `chainId === DEFAULT_CHAIN.id`, otherwise ConnectWallet.
- `EnsureAuth.tsx`: Atlas sign-in button with info, success and error toasts.

**Transaction buttons**
- There is no shared TransactionButton. Buttons are the ui-lib `Button` with `isLoading`/`disabled` from simulate state.
- `ErrorButtonMessage.tsx` + `StyledIcons/ClosedCircleIcon` render the error text below.
- `TxnHash.tsx` renders an explorer link.
- `LightButton.tsx` and `DottedMenuButton.tsx` are button variants.

**Loading and misc**
- `StyledSkeleton.tsx`: `StyledSkeleton` plus the `SkeletonDisputeCard`, `SkeletonDisputeListItem`/`SkeletonDisputeListRow`, `SkeletonVoteCard` and `SkeletonEvidenceCard` presets.
- `Loader.tsx`, `Spinner.tsx`.
- `ScrollTop.tsx`, `HeroImage.tsx`, `Phase.tsx` (sortition phase display), `NumberInputField.tsx`, `LabeledInput.tsx`, `PlusMinusField.tsx`, `InternalLink.tsx`, `ExternalLink.tsx`, `JurorLink.tsx`.

---

## 3. Staking flow

**Files**
- `src/pages/Courts/CourtDetails/StakePanel/index.tsx`: Stake/Withdraw tags, then `InputDisplay`, then `Simulator`.
- `StakePanel/InputDisplay.tsx`: input and client-side validation.
- `StakePanel/StakeWithdrawButton.tsx`: the approve/setStake orchestration.
- `StakePanel/StakeWithdrawPopup/{index,Header,stakeSteps}.tsx`: timeline popup.
- `StakePanel/Simulator/`: reward projection using `useJurorStakeDetailsQuery`, `useHomePageExtraStats(30)` and `useCoinPrice`.
- Hooks: `src/hooks/usePNKData.tsx`, `src/hooks/useSortitionModule.ts`, `src/hooks/useParsedAmount.ts`.
- Utils: `src/utils/parseWagmiError.ts`, `src/utils/refecthWithRetry.ts` (typo in the filename is real).
- Maintenance: `src/pages/Courts/StakeMaintenanceButton/{index,PassPhaseButton,ExecuteDelayedStakeButton}.tsx`.

**Data (`usePnkData({courtId})`)**
- `PNK.balanceOf`.
- `SortitionModule.getJurorBalance(addr, courtId)` returns `[totalStaked, totalLocked, stakedInCourt, nbCourts]`. The UI uses **`[2]`**.
- `PNK.allowance(addr, KlerosCore)`.
- All three poll with `REFETCH_INTERVAL`.

**Validation (`InputDisplay`)**
- The amount is debounced 500 ms, then converted with `useParsedAmount` (`parseUnits(...,18)`).
- Error messages: zero PNK balance, insufficient balance, insufficient staked amount (withdraw), or below `court.minStake`, where the check is current in-court stake plus the amount.
- The field shows `errorMsg` unless the popup is open.

**Orchestration (`StakeWithdrawButton`)**
- `isAllowance = isStaking && allowance < parsedAmount`.
- `targetStake` is the absolute new stake passed to `setStake`: `stakedInCourt ± parsedAmount`. When `isAllowance` is true it is just `parsedAmount`, used for the approval delta.
- Approval: `useSimulatePnkIncreaseAllowance([KlerosCore, targetStake - allowance])` and `useWritePnkIncreaseAllowance`.
- Stake: `useSimulateKlerosCoreSetStake([courtId, targetStake])` (disabled while an approval is needed) and `useWriteKlerosCoreSetStake`.
- Click flow:
  1. Approve, then wait for 2 confirmations.
  2. `refetchAllowance()`, then `refetchWithRetry(refetchSetStake)`, a workaround for TanStack issue #8209.
  3. `handleStake`: write, then wait for 2 confirmations.
  4. Popup steps come from `getStakeSteps(StakeSteps.X, …)`.
- An `AbortController` drops state updates after the popup closes.
- Simulate errors: `parseWagmiError` (metaMessages[0], else shortMessage, else message) goes into `setErrorMsg`.
- `isDisabled` is true when:
  - the amount is 0, or
  - it would end below minStake, or
  - the relevant simulation is missing, loading or errored.
- The button is wrapped in `EnsureChain` and carries `data-testId="stake-withdraw-button"` for e2e.

**Delayed stakes**
- The SortitionModule delays `setStake` on-chain outside the staking phase.
- The frontend has **no user-facing "your stake is delayed" messaging**. A grep for "delayed" outside generated code only hits the maintenance hooks and button.
- `ExecuteDelayedStakeButton` is enabled when `phase === staking && writeIndex >= readIndex`. It calls `executeDelayedStakes(1 + write - read)` through the generic `useSimulateSortitionModule`/`useWriteSortitionModule` with `@ts-ignore`. `useSortitionModule.ts` also uses `@ts-ignore` on every `functionName`.

**Things to watch in review**
- The popup reads `refetchSetStake` right after the approval. Whether its args are already the post-approval `targetStake` depends on a re-render having happened first.
- Stake history (`useStakingEventsByCourt`) comes from Atlas, not the subgraph, and is disabled on local deployment.
- e2e coverage: `src/tests/e2e/stake.spec.ts` covers approve + stake.

---

## 4. Tests

**Vitest** (`web/vitest.config.ts`)
- Config: jsdom, globals, `vite-tsconfig-paths`, `include: src/**/*.test.ts(x)`, v8 coverage.
- Setup `src/test/setup.ts`: localStorage mock, cleared in `beforeEach` along with `vi.clearAllMocks()`, and `vi.unstubAllEnvs()` in `afterAll`. It also loads `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest`.
- Test doubles: `src/test/mocks/{index,contracts}.ts` (mock DK ABIs and addresses, used in `vi.mock("hooks/contracts/generated")`) and `src/test/fakes/shutter.ts` (deterministic fake encrypt; its TODO says it is not yet verified against the real API).
- Scripts: `yarn test`, `test:watch`, `test:coverage`.

**Unit-tested today** (mostly the pure transaction-building layer, only 1 component test)
- `src/actions/commit/builders/{classic,gated,shutter}.builder.test.ts`
- `src/actions/reveal/builders/{classic,gated,shutter}.builder.test.ts`
- `src/actions/reveal/{resolveRevealInputs.test.ts, resolveRevealInputs.integration.test.ts}`
- `src/actions/reveal/helpers/bruteForceChoice.test.ts`
- `src/actions/vote/builders/classic.builder.test.ts`
- `src/actions/fundAppeal/builders/classic.builder.test.ts`
- `src/actions/helpers/storage/{storage,getVoteKey}.test.ts`
- `src/utils/crypto/{hashVote,hashJustification,generateSalt}.test.ts`
- `src/utils/urlValidation.test.ts`
- `src/dispute-kits/prepareArbitratorExtradata.test.ts`
- `src/pages/Cases/CaseDetails/Voting/Shutter/Reveal.test.tsx`: the only component test. It is new on this branch (`e19cf9f1`) and mocks hooks, router, i18n, the ui-lib, and `src/dispute-kits` → `disputeKits`.

Gaps: there are no tests for the ArgentinaConsumerProtection or ClassicUniversity builders, the staking flow, `disputeFeature.ts` selection logic, `NewDisputeContext`, or any hooks.

**Gotchas for tests**
- `src/dispute-kits/index.ts` notes that tests mocking `generated` must import `DisputeKits` from `./disputeKits` so the registry does not load.
- Importing `src/utils` pulls in `@kleros/kleros-app`, whose `module` points to `dist/`, and `dist/` is not built locally. On this branch `Reveal.tsx` therefore replaced `isUndefined` with an inline `=== undefined || === null` check. That departs from the convention and is worth a look.

**Playwright e2e**
- Config `web/playwright.config.ts`: `testDir: ./src/tests`, chromium only, `baseURL: http://localhost:5173/#`, locale en-US, not fully parallel, no `webServer` (commented out).
- Specs in `src/tests/e2e/`: `smoke`, `wallet`, `stake`, `case` (create case), and `voting` (stake, create case, pass to Drawing, draw, pass period, vote). The voting spec has a TODO: no DK-specific or hidden-vote flows yet.
- Fixtures in `fixtures/` are merged in `index.ts`:
  - `wallet.ts` calls `window._setupMockAccount` (exposed by `src/context/Web3Provider.tsx` using `createMockAdapter` in `src/config/wagmi.ts`), then clicks "Connect" and "Mock Connector".
  - `hardhat.ts` is a viem test client on the local hardhat chain.
  - `time.ts` syncs the Playwright clock with the hardhat timestamp.
  - `atlas.ts` mocks the Atlas `/graphql` endpoint (GetNonce, Login with a test JWT via `utils/jwt.ts`).
- Chain manipulation helpers: `utils/{setupStake,setupCase,passToPhase}.ts` and `utils/dispute/*`.
- **Requires the full local stack**, set up manually per the root `README.md`:
  - hardhat node with contracts deployed (`yarn workspace @kleros/kleros-v2-contracts start-local`)
  - local graph-node subgraph (`start-local-indexer`)
  - Vite dev server via `yarn start-local` on :5173, using `.env.local.public`
  - generated hooks and GraphQL for chain `localhost`
- Note: `window._setupMockAccount` is attached **unconditionally** (not gated to local deployment). Worth flagging.

**CI does not run web tests (verified)**
- `.github/workflows/`: `codeql`, `contracts-testing`, `dependency-review`, `deploy-bots`, `deploy-subgraph`, `scorecards`, `sentry-release`, `sonarcloud`.
  - `contracts-testing.yml` runs `yarn test` only in `contracts/`, and `paths-ignore`s `web/**` on push.
  - `sentry-release.yml` only builds web (`yarn build:web:ci`) on master.
  - `sonarcloud.yml` is a scan only.
- Netlify (`web/netlify.toml`) only builds.
- No vitest or playwright runs anywhere.
- Local guard: `.husky/pre-commit` runs `check-types` for web when web files are staged, plus `lint-staged` (`eslint --fix` + prettier).

---

## 5. Conventions

**Naming and layout**
- PascalCase folders for pages and components, with `index.tsx` as the entry.
- Sub-parts sit as siblings: `Header.tsx`, `Desktop*/Mobile*` pairs such as `TopJurors/JurorCard/{DesktopCard,MobileCard}.tsx`.
- Hooks are `useX.ts(x)` in `src/hooks`. GraphQL hooks go in `src/hooks/queries/useXQuery.ts`: `useQuery` + `graphqlBatcher.fetch({id: crypto.randomUUID(), document, variables})` + `REFETCH_INTERVAL`/`STALE_TIME`.
- Transaction logic is in `src/actions/{commit,reveal,vote,fundAppeal}/`:
  - `params.ts`, `context.ts` and `execute.ts`.
  - `builders/` holds a `Record<DisputeKits, Builder>` map built with `defineActionBuilder` from `actions/helpers/builder.ts`, with injectable deps for tests.
  - These are consumed by `useMutation` hooks: `hooks/useVote.ts`, `useCastCommit.tsx`, `useRevealVote.ts`, `useFundAppeal.ts`.

**Component structure**
- Order within a file: imports, then styled-components (often `landscapeStyle(() => css\`...\`)`), then the `interface IProps`, then `const X: React.FC<IProps> = (...) => {}`.
- Inside the component: `useTranslation`, router hooks, data hooks, `useMemo`/`useCallback`, then JSX.
- Default export at the bottom.
- Props are often spread as `{...{ a, b }}`.

**Path aliases** (`web/tsconfig.json` `paths`, `vite-tsconfig-paths`)
- `src`, `utils`, `actions`, `assets`, `components`, `context`, `layout`, `consts`, `hooks`, `queries` (= `src/hooks/queries`), `pages`, `styles`, `svgs`.
- The `~` prefix is banned (`no-restricted-imports`).

**Import order** (`web/eslint.config.mjs` `import/order`, warn level, alphabetized, with newlines between groups)
1. react / styled-components
2. externals
3. `@kleros/**`
4. `svgs/assets`
5. `hooks/utils/consts/context`
6. `queries`
7. `src/**`
8. `styles`
9. `layout/pages/components`
10. relative imports

Other lint rules: max-len 120 (warn), `no-console` except warn/error/info/debug, `no-explicit-any` and non-null assertions allowed, `eslint-plugin-security`.

**Mixed import styles you will see side by side**
- `isUndefined` is imported from `utils/index` (75 places) and from `src/utils` (41).

## 1. Feature pages (`src/pages`)

- `StakePanel/StakeWithdrawButton.tsx`: the approve/setStake orchestration.
- `StakePanel/StakeWithdrawPopup/{index,Header,stakeSteps}.tsx`: timeline popup.
- `StakePanel/Simulator/`: reward projection using `useJurorStakeDetailsQuery`, `useHomePageExtraStats(30)` and `useCoinPrice`.
- Hooks: `src/hooks/usePNKData.tsx`, `src/hooks/useSortitionModule.ts`, `src/hooks/useParsedAmount.ts`.
- Utils: `src/utils/parseWagmiError.ts`, `src/utils/refecthWithRetry.ts` (typo in the filename is real).
- Maintenance: `src/pages/Courts/StakeMaintenanceButton/{index,PassPhaseButton,ExecuteDelayedStakeButton}.tsx`.

**Data (`usePnkData({courtId})`)**
- `PNK.balanceOf`.
- `SortitionModule.getJurorBalance(addr, courtId)` returns `[totalStaked, totalLocked, stakedInCourt, nbCourts]`. The UI uses **`[2]`**.
- `PNK.allowance(addr, KlerosCore)`.
- All three poll with `REFETCH_INTERVAL`.

**Validation (`InputDisplay`)**
- The amount is debounced 500 ms, then converted with `useParsedAmount` (`parseUnits(...,18)`).
- Error messages: zero PNK balance, insufficient balance, insufficient staked amount (withdraw), or below `court.minStake`, where the check is current in-court stake plus the amount.
- The field shows `errorMsg` unless the popup is open.

**Orchestration (`StakeWithdrawButton`)**
- `isAllowance = isStaking && allowance < parsedAmount`.
- `targetStake` is the absolute new stake passed to `setStake`: `stakedInCourt ± parsedAmount`. When `isAllowance` is true it is just `parsedAmount`, used for the approval delta.
- Approval: `useSimulatePnkIncreaseAllowance([KlerosCore, targetStake - allowance])` and `useWritePnkIncreaseAllowance`.
- Stake: `useSimulateKlerosCoreSetStake([courtId, targetStake])` (disabled while an approval is needed) and `useWriteKlerosCoreSetStake`.
- Click flow:
  1. Approve, then wait for 2 confirmations.
  2. `refetchAllowance()`, then `refetchWithRetry(refetchSetStake)`, a workaround for TanStack issue #8209.
  3. `handleStake`: write, then wait for 2 confirmations.
  4. Popup steps come from `getStakeSteps(StakeSteps.X, …)`.
- An `AbortController` drops state updates after the popup closes.
- Simulate errors: `parseWagmiError` (metaMessages[0], else shortMessage, else message) goes into `setErrorMsg`.
- `isDisabled` is true when:
  - the amount is 0, or
  - it would end below minStake, or
  - the relevant simulation is missing, loading or errored.
- The button is wrapped in `EnsureChain` and carries `data-testId="stake-withdraw-button"` for e2e.

**Delayed stakes**
- The SortitionModule delays `setStake` on-chain outside the staking phase.
- The frontend has **no user-facing "your stake is delayed" messaging**. A grep for "delayed" outside generated code only hits the maintenance hooks and button.
- `ExecuteDelayedStakeButton` is enabled when `phase === staking && writeIndex >= readIndex`. It calls `executeDelayedStakes(1 + write - read)` through the generic `useSimulateSortitionModule`/`useWriteSortitionModule` with `@ts-ignore`. `useSortitionModule.ts` also uses `@ts-ignore` on every `functionName`.

**Things to watch in review**
- The popup reads `refetchSetStake` right after the approval. Whether its args are already the post-approval `targetStake` depends on a re-render having happened first.
- Stake history (`useStakingEventsByCourt`) comes from Atlas, not the subgraph, and is disabled on local deployment.
- e2e coverage: `src/tests/e2e/stake.spec.ts` covers approve + stake.

- Sub-parts sit as siblings: `Header.tsx`, `Desktop*/Mobile*` pairs such as `TopJurors/JurorCard/{DesktopCard,MobileCard}.tsx`.

- Transaction logic is in `src/actions/{commit,reveal,vote,fundAppeal}/`:

  - `builders/` holds a `Record<DisputeKits, Builder>` map built with `defineActionBuilder` from `actions/helpers/builder.ts`, with injectable deps for tests.
  - These are consumed by `useMutation` hooks: `hooks/useVote.ts`, `useCastCommit.tsx`, `useRevealVote.ts`, `useFundAppeal.ts`.

**Component structure**
- Order within a file: imports, then styled-components (often `landscapeStyle(() => css\`...\`)`), then the `interface IProps`, then `const X: React.FC<IProps> = (...) => {}`.
- Inside the component: `useTranslation`, router hooks, data hooks, `useMemo`/`useCallback`, then JSX.
- Default export at the bottom.
- Props are often spread as `{...{ a, b }}`.

**Path aliases** (`web/tsconfig.json` `paths`, `vite-tsconfig-paths`)
- `src`, `utils`, `actions`, `assets`, `components`, `context`, `layout`, `consts`, `hooks`, `queries` (= `src/hooks/queries`), `pages`, `styles`, `svgs`.
- The `~` prefix is banned (`no-restricted-imports`).

**Import order** (`web/eslint.config.mjs` `import/order`, warn level, alphabetized, with newlines between groups)
1. react / styled-components
2. externals
3. `@kleros/**`
4. `svgs/assets`
5. `hooks/utils/consts/context`
6. `queries`
7. `src/**`
8. `styles`

**Where the code differs from the brief:**
- **No Dashboard page.** It is now the Profile page at `/profile`, with stakes, cases and votes tabs.
- **No ui-components-library v3 or Tailwind here.** The library is `^2.20.0` on `dev` and on this branch. The v3 migration is only on `origin/feat/file-viewer-from-ui-components-library` (about 134 files, last updated 2026-09-10), so expect big conflicts when it merges.

**Risks worth checking in review:**
- **Evidence tab data can go stale.** The tab renders without the `arbitrable` address. The cache key for the populated dispute data leaves that address out and never expires, so the Evidence and Overview tabs share one entry and whichever loads first wins.
- **Delayed stakes are invisible to users.** Outside the staking phase the contract delays a stake, but the UI never says so. The only related control is the "execute delayed stakes" button in the court maintenance menu.
- **Stake right after approval may use stale data.** After an approval, the staking flow re-runs the stake check straight away. Whether it has the new amount depends on React having re-rendered first.
- **Test-only wallet hook exposed in all builds.** `window._setupMockAccount` (used by the e2e tests) is attached on every deployment, not just local.
- **This branch drops a convention to make a test load.** The only commit on it (`e19cf9f1`) replaces `isUndefined` in Shutter `Reveal.tsx` with an inline null check, because importing `src/utils` pulls in `@kleros/kleros-app`, whose `dist/` isn't built locally. That same commit adds the only component test in the repo.
- **Generated code isn't committed.** The contract hooks and GraphQL types are gitignored and currently missing, so run `yarn generate` before type-checking or testing.

The report also covers:
- each page's purpose, components and hooks;
- one line per shared component;
- the full stake and withdraw flow, with file paths;
- which unit tests exist and the gaps: no staking, feature-selection or hook tests;
- the lint rules and conventions;
